claimBoundary: This model inventories repository-mounted experience structure and defines falsifiable UIUX rationalization requirements. It does not prove aesthetic quality, representative usability, assistive-technology usability, deployment behavior, legal compliance, or enterprise readiness.

mountGraph.diagnosticRule: installer count is diagnostic, not a quality KPI; persistent semantic/presentation ownership per slot must converge to one
mountGraph.risk: historical and feature enhancers can layer markup/copy/styles before final constitutional convergence

surfaceInventory.specificity: requirement, scope basis, mapping, gap, next decision
owner, due date, execution, closure verification
scenario, human rating, treatment, review date

commonGrammar.cardUsePolicy: cards are reserved for a single decision/narrative object or semantically grouped summary; repeated registries default to dense rows
commonGrammar.singleRowRule: compress labels, state, owner/due and CTA into one row when legible; overflow moves to progressive detail, never by deleting epistemically material fields
commonGrammar.responsiveRule: semantic order remains invariant; visual rows may wrap or stack without changing authority, state or action meaning
commonGrammar.tokenRule: common visual tokens and primitive geometry are centrally owned; procedure-specific modules may specialize content density but may not fork the design system

home: show at most three compact priority rows
move explanation/trust detail behind disclosure except the immediate reason
processes: replace oversized catalogue cards with compact procedure rows/tiles
one code, title, one-line purpose and route action
no second explanatory paragraph per procedure
monitoring: common procedure frame is the only page identity
monitor register and source register use dense rows
add-material is the primary work entry, plan creation is secondary/disclosed
incidents: common procedure frame is the only page identity
narrative remains expandable because it is semantically material
objects: surface owner, source and reattestation state inline
details open only for extended metadata/evidence
coverage: scope basis and unresolved gap remain visible
never render coverage as conformity score
actions: owner, due date, execution state and closure-verification state stay distinct
CTA aligned on same row where legible
risks: rating is not status and not objective probability
review/treatment action remains distinct from severity
assurance: answer version and evidence basis remain visible when decision-relevant
internal approval never styled as independent assurance
admin: technical readiness and diagnostic evidence progressive by default
epistemic: search, primary mode and essential filter occupy one toolbar row when width permits
advanced filters and technical modes remain progressive
relation list is default; graph is an optional analytical mode
proof: secondary domains become compact accordion rows
avoid nine visually equivalent stacked panels
ai-settings: provider, model and key-environment contract remain on the first plane
advanced AI instructions remain behind disclosure
one save action; no visual treatment implies AI decision authority

trajectoryDecision.strategy: embed UIUX obligations into SCOPE-0/REALITY-0/DECIDE-0 and add one post-DECIDE implementation barrier UIUX-CONVERGE-0 before S4-A6-CLOSE
trajectoryDecision.conditionalRelationship: C5-SEMANTIC-OWNER-COMPRESSION is eligible now and must be terminal before UIUX-CONVERGE-0 may claim owner convergence; C1-C5 still must all be terminal before S4-A6-CLOSE

rejectedAlternatives.reason: duplicates the cognition already owned by SCOPE-0, REALITY-0 and DECIDE-0
creates governance serialization without semantic necessity; procedure specializations are work units under one convergence contract
C5 owns semantic owner contraction, not target experience, density grammar or procedure-specific presentation
closure must verify convergence, not discover or implement the experience architecture
would encode unproven operator, client and density assumptions into presentation
